title: Repositories
subtitle: Where backups are stored, whether every repository works, and how much is stored.

noTenant.title: No tenant selected
noTenant.description: Select a tenant in the top bar to manage its repositories.

role.primaryHint: Backups are written here first; restores read from here.
role.copyHint: Every new backup is also written here. Data from before the copy existed is mirrored and verified by the copy run.
role.previousHint: Retired: no longer written to. Kept until removed; restore, checks, downloads and later backups of objects protected before the switch still read from it whenever a restore point lives only here.
role.replacePrimaryHint: Choose below whether existing backups move to the new repository first, or stay where they are.

usage.title: Usage
usage.description: Protected data compared with what the deduplicated, encrypted store takes.
usage.logicalHint: {count, plural, =0 {No completed backup yet} one {Latest backup of # object} other {Latest backups of # objects}}
usage.logicalHintRepositories: {count, plural, =0 {Machines, file shares and containers not included} one {Latest backup of # object, without machines, file shares and containers} other {Latest backups of # objects, without machines, file shares and containers}}
usage.physicalHint: {count, plural, one {# pack} other {# packs}} in the chunk store
usage.physicalHintRepositories: {count, plural, one {# pack} other {# packs}} in the chunk store, {bytes} in restic repositories
usage.savingsHint: Against {bytes} in {count, plural, one {# retained backup} other {# retained backups}}
usage.growthNoBaseline: The chunk store held nothing before this period
usage.empty: Nothing stored yet. The chart fills in with the first backup.
usage.emptyChunkStore: The chunk store holds nothing yet. Machines, file shares and containers back up into restic repositories, counted under Stored; the chart follows the chunk store.
usage.growthNote: Growth counts the data stored in the chunk store today by the day it was written. Space freed by cleanup does not show as a decline. The restic repositories of machines, file shares and containers keep no history and are not part of it.
usage.chartLabel: Chunk store from {from} to {to}: {start} at the start, {end} at the end

targets.title: Repositories
targets.description: The primary receives every backup first; copies receive the same data at another location.
targets.managedByProvider: Server paths are managed by the provider admin.
targets.retiredLocation: Stands in for the environment's default repository from before it was replaced. It has no location of its own to test.
targets.insecureEndpoint: This repository uses plain HTTP: access keys and backups travel unencrypted. {appName} keeps using it, but saving it again requires an https:// endpoint. Switch the storage service to HTTPS and change the endpoint.

singleLocation.title: Only one repository
singleLocation.description: All backups of this tenant are stored in one place. Add a copy repository somewhere else, such as offsite object storage, so a single failure cannot take every copy (3-2-1 rule).

targets.systemDisk: On the system disk of the {appName} server, under the operating system, Docker and the database. When backups fill it, {appName} stops. Use a second disk, a network share or object storage.

default.name: Installation default
default.description: Set by the provider for this installation; used while this tenant has no primary repository of its own.
default.copy: Every write is also copied to a second path on the server.
default.copyAt: Every write is also copied to {location}.
default.notChecked: Not tested in this session. The installation default keeps no test history.

misconfigured.title: Installation default repository is misconfigured
misconfigured.description: The installation's default repository is not usable. This tenant's backups cannot be written until the provider fixes it or a primary repository is added.

default.inUse: Selected: new backups of this tenant go here. To use a repository of its own instead, add one with the role "Primary".
default.notInUse: Not in use: this tenant has a primary repository of its own.
default.backBlocked: Going back to the installation default is not possible once backups exist in the tenant's own repository: {appName} cannot move them there yet. They stay where they are.

use.title: Use the installation default?
use.description: {name} is removed as the primary repository, and new backups of this tenant go to the installation default. Nothing is stored in {name} yet.

health.notTested: Not tested yet. Run a test before relying on this repository.
health.configInvalid: The stored settings are no longer valid. Edit the repository.

errors.path_missing: The directory does not exist. Mount the network share or create the directory first.
errors.not_a_directory: The path is not a directory.
errors.not_writable: {appName} cannot write here (permissions or a read-only mount).
errors.access_denied: Access denied: the key lacks permission for this bucket.
errors.invalid_credentials: The access key or the secret is not accepted.
errors.wrong_region: The bucket is in another region, or the endpoint does not match it.
errors.unreachable: The storage service is not reachable (DNS, network or firewall).
errors.tls: The TLS certificate of the endpoint is not trusted.
errors.timeout: The storage did not answer in time.
errors.integrity: The data read back differs from what was written.

warnings.ephemeral_path: This directory is inside the container, not on a volume or mount. Its data is lost when the container is recreated.
warnings.insecure_endpoint: The endpoint uses plain HTTP: credentials and data travel unencrypted.
warnings.cleanup_failed: The small test object could not be deleted again. It lies in the tenant's probes folder and can be removed by hand.

objectLock.filesystemHint: A filesystem cannot enforce immutability: anyone with access to the server can change or delete files. An archive in this repository is protected by {appName} and the hash chain only.
objectLock.notCheckedHint: A successful test also detects whether the bucket enforces Object Lock (WORM).
objectLock.enabledHint: The bucket enforces retention: locked objects cannot be changed or deleted before their date. Whether backups are locked is set under Immutable backups below; for the archive, {appName} locks the archive item records.
objectLock.disabledHint: Backups on this bucket cannot be made immutable. An archive on this bucket is protected by {appName} and the hash chain only. Object Lock can only be switched on when a bucket is created.
objectLock.unsupported: Object Lock not supported by this provider
objectLock.unsupportedHint: Backups in this repository cannot be made immutable. An archive in this repository is protected by {appName} and the hash chain only.
objectLock.unknownAccessHint: The key may not read the bucket's Object Lock configuration (s3:GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration).
objectLock.unknownErrorHint: The provider did not answer the Object Lock query. Test again later.

retention.days: {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} retention
retention.years: {count, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} retention

objectLock.retiredHint: This placeholder stands for the environment's storage settings from before they were replaced; it was never tested on its own.

migration.failedSource: Replacement failed; this location is still the primary
migration.cancelledSource: Replacement cancelled; this location is still the primary
migration.stalled: Migration stalled; cancel to finalize it
migration.stalledSource: Replacement stalled; this location is still the primary
migration.cancelConfirmDescription: Copying stops at the next checkpoint. Nothing is lost: the old primary keeps serving backups and restores, and this repository stays a copy you can remove or try again with.

description.s3: A bucket at Hetzner Object Storage, Amazon S3, Wasabi, Backblaze B2, Garage or another S3-compatible service. Credentials are stored encrypted.
description.local: A directory inside the containers: the default volume or an NFS network share mounted into the api and worker containers.

form.name: Name

namePlaceholder.local: e.g. NAS in the server room

primaryBlocked.primaryExists: This tenant already has a primary. Add a copy and promote it later, or choose "Replace the primary" above.
primaryBlocked.tenantHasData: This tenant already has backups on the installation default. Add a copy and promote it later, or choose "Replace the primary" above.

form.migrationModeMoveHint: A background run copies every pack, manifest and key, and the backup repositories of containers, machines and file shares, to the new repository and verifies them by hash, then switches the primary automatically. The old location stays in place, read-only, until you remove it.
form.migrationModeKeep: Keep existing backups where they are
form.migrationModeKeepHint: The new repository becomes primary right away, nothing is copied. The old location stays in place, read-only: restoring, checking and backing up objects from before the switch keep working by reading it, but every new byte is written to the new repository only. A standalone restore (restow-restore) needs both locations passed to --storage for a snapshot from after this switch.

local.basePathHint: Absolute path in the containers. The directory must exist and be writable.

s3.presetHint: Fills in endpoint, region and addressing. Adjust them to where your bucket is.
s3.prefixHint: Keeps {appName} data in a folder of the bucket.
s3.insecureEndpoint: This endpoint uses plain HTTP. Credentials and backups travel unencrypted; use HTTPS unless the service sits on a trusted internal network.
s3.forcePathStyleHint: Needed by Garage and many self-hosted services.
s3.keepCredentials: Leave both fields empty to keep the stored key (…{hint}).
s3.secretHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
s3.credentialsAgain: The endpoint changed, so the stored key is not sent there. Enter the key pair again.

testHint.s3: Writes, reads and deletes a small test object and checks Object Lock. Nothing is saved.
testHint.local: Checks the directory, then writes, reads and deletes a small test file. Nothing is saved.

form.migrationModeKeepBlocked: Not available: containers or file shares of this tenant have backup repositories on the current primary, and they would stay behind. Choose "Move existing backups".

validation.invalid_characters: Contains characters that are not allowed.
validation.absolute_path: Enter an absolute path starting with /.
validation.path_traversal: The path must not contain . or .. segments.
validation.root_path: The root directory cannot be a repository.
validation.system_path: System directories cannot be used as repositories.
validation.bucket_name: 3 to 63 characters: lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
validation.prefix: Letters, digits, dots, underscores, hyphens and slashes only, without empty, . or .. segments.
validation.endpoint_url: Enter a complete URL, e.g. https://fsn1.your-objectstorage.com.
validation.endpoint_protocol: The endpoint must start with https://.
validation.endpoint_insecure: {appName} only connects to S3 over HTTPS: enter an https:// endpoint. Plain http:// is only possible on this machine (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]).
validation.endpoint_path: Enter only the service address, without a path or bucket name.
validation.endpoint_credentials: The endpoint must not contain a user name or password.
validation.region: Letters, digits, hyphens and underscores only.
validation.private_address: The endpoint points into a private or local network.
validation.local_hostname: Use the public host name of the service.
validation.unresolvable: This host name does not resolve.
validation.credentials_pair: Enter both the access key ID and the secret, or neither to keep the stored key.
validation.credentials_again: The endpoint changed: enter the key pair again.
validation.whitespace: Must not contain spaces or line breaks.

completeness.title: Check copy {name}
completeness.description: Compares the copy with the primary: every pack, backup manifest and key must be present.
completeness.checking: Comparing the copy with the primary …

complete.title: The copy is complete
complete.description: Everything the primary holds is present on this copy.

incomplete.title: The copy is not complete yet
incomplete.description: {bytes} of backup data is still missing. The copy run mirrors it; new backups reach the copy right away.

completeness.listingOnly: Presence is checked by listing. The copy run and the storage check verify contents by checksum.

promote.title: Make {name} the primary
promote.description: The current primary becomes a copy and keeps receiving every backup. From now on, restores read from this repository first.
promote.descriptionFromDefault: From now on, backups and restores use this repository first, and this tenant stops using the installation default. Data already stored there stays until the provider removes it.

notVerified.title: Test the repository first
notVerified.description: Only a repository whose last test succeeded can become the primary.

promote.effect: Everything is in place. The switch applies to the next backup and restore.

delete.title: Remove {name}?
delete.description: {appName} stops writing backups to this copy.
delete.descriptionPrimary: {appName} stops using this repository. Without a primary repository of its own, this tenant uses the installation default again.
delete.descriptionPrevious: This location was replaced as the primary. Removing it means older backups that live only here are no longer restorable, checkable or searchable.
delete.dataStays: Data already stored at this location is not deleted. Remove it at the storage provider if it is no longer needed.

toasts.migrationRetried: The migration to {name} was queued again.
toasts.defaultSelected: This tenant uses the installation default again.

errors.localRequiresProviderAdmin: Only a provider admin can manage server paths.
errors.primaryExists: This tenant already has a primary repository. Add a copy and make it the primary once it is complete.
errors.tenantHasData: This tenant already has backups. Add the new location as a copy; once it is complete, make it the primary.
errors.locationOverlap: This location is already in use by this tenant, or lies inside one that is.
errors.locationLocked: The primary holds backups, so its location cannot change. Add the new location as a copy and make it the primary once it is complete.
errors.primaryHoldsData: The primary holds backups and cannot be removed. Make another repository the primary first.
errors.alreadyPrimary: This repository already is the primary.
errors.notVerified: Test the repository successfully before making it the primary.
errors.copyIncomplete: The copy is not complete yet.
errors.invalidLocation: The location is not valid. Check the marked fields.
errors.endpointNotAllowed: This endpoint is not allowed. Tenant admins can only use public HTTPS endpoints.
errors.configInvalid: The stored settings of this repository are no longer valid. Edit the repository.
errors.credentialsUnusable: The stored credentials cannot be read. Enter them again.
errors.defaultMisconfigured: The installation default repository is misconfigured on the server.
errors.unreachable: The primary or the copy could not be listed. Test both repositories.
errors.masterKeyMissing: The server has no master key (RESTOW_MASTER_KEY), so credentials cannot be stored.
errors.migrationInProgress: This tenant already has a storage migration running. Wait for it to finish or cancel it.
errors.notACopy: Only a copy repository can be promoted to primary.
errors.migrationNotFound: This repository has no storage migration to cancel.
errors.migrationNotCancellable: This migration already finished and cannot be cancelled.
errors.migrationNotRetryable: Only a failed move can be tried again.
errors.keepTargetUnreachable: The new repository could not be confirmed with a quick write, read and delete check. Fix the location or credentials, or choose "move" instead.
errors.keepBlockedByActiveJob: A backup, archive, retention, storage check or storage migration run for this tenant is still waiting or running. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
errors.previousHoldsExclusiveData: This location still holds backup data no other repository has. Run a "move" replacement first to copy it onto the current primary, then remove this location.
errors.installationDefaultReadonly: This placeholder stands for a retired installation default and has no settings of its own.
errors.queueNotReady: The background run queue is not ready yet. Try again in a moment.
errors.activeEndpoints: Servers or clients back up to this storage through the agent, and a change of the primary does not move their backups yet. Revoke or uninstall those machines first; their existing backups stay readable from the old location, which has to stay attached.
errors.previousHoldsEndpointRepositories: This location still holds backup repositories (of a server or client, a container or a file share) that only it has. Replace the primary with "move" to copy them onto it, or keep this location attached.
errors.immutabilityObjectLockUnavailable: This bucket does not enforce Object Lock, so its backups cannot be made immutable. Object Lock can only be enabled when a bucket is created.
errors.immutabilityLoweringForbidden: Only the provider owner can lower or switch off immutability.
errors.immutabilityModeNotAvailable: This mode is not available for this kind of repository.
errors.immutabilityNotWritable: Nothing is written to this location any more; immutability applies to what is written from now on.
errors.immutabilityNotObjectLock: Only a repository with Object Lock is checked with the storage.
errors.switchBlockedByRepositories: Containers or file shares of this tenant have backup repositories on the current primary. Keeping existing backups where they are, or promoting a copy, would leave those repositories behind, and their next backups would fail or begin from scratch. Replace the primary with "move" instead: it copies the repositories and verifies them before it switches.

immutability.title: Immutable backups
immutability.offObjectLockHint: The bucket enforces Object Lock: backups written here can be locked so that nobody can delete or change them before a date.
immutability.offNoObjectLockHint: This bucket has no Object Lock, so anyone holding its access key can delete the backups in it. Object Lock can only be enabled when a bucket is created: add a bucket with Object Lock as a repository or as a copy.
immutability.offDirectoryHint: A directory cannot be made immutable: anyone with access to the server or the share can delete its files. A deletion delay can at least keep {appName} itself from deleting backups too early.
immutability.complianceOn: Immutable: Object Lock, compliance mode, {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
immutability.complianceOnHint: New backup data is locked by the storage itself. Nobody can delete or change it before its date: not {appName}, not someone holding its access key, not an administrator, not the owner of the bucket.
immutability.governanceOn: Immutable: Object Lock, governance mode, {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
immutability.governanceOnHint: New backup data is locked by the storage itself. An account with the s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission can still lift the lock; {appName} never uses it. Give its access key no such permission, or choose compliance mode.
immutability.deletionDelayOn: Deletion delay, {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} (not immutable)
immutability.deletionDelayOnHint: {appName} refuses to delete or overwrite backup files before they are {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} old. This protects against misuse of {appName}, such as a stolen administrator account or a shortened retention policy. Someone with access to the server or the share can still delete the files.
immutability.unlockedFound: Of {sampled} sampled objects, {count, plural, one {# was} other {# were}} written without lock. New backups may not be protected: check the storage and its access key.
immutability.weakerModeFound: {count, plural, one {# sampled object is} other {# sampled objects are}} locked in governance mode only, although compliance mode is set.
immutability.renewalOverdue: The renewal of the locks is overdue: data that new backups reuse may be locked for less than {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. The daily retention job renews them.
immutability.renewalFailed: {count, plural, one {The lock of # object could not be renewed.} other {The locks of # objects could not be renewed.}}
immutability.renewedAt: Locks of the data in use renewed {date}.
immutability.notRenewedYet: The locks of older data in use are not renewed yet; the daily retention job does it.
immutability.verifiedAt: Checked with the storage {date}: {locked} of {sampled} sampled objects locked.
immutability.deferred: {count, plural, one {# deletion waits} other {# deletions wait}} for its lock to run out.
immutability.verifyFoundUnlocked: {count, plural, one {# sampled object is not locked.} other {# sampled objects are not locked.}}

modes.offHint: Backups can be deleted before their retention ends.
modes.complianceHint: Nobody can shorten or lift the lock, not even the owner of the bucket. Recommended.
modes.governanceHint: An account with the bypass permission can lift the lock.
modes.delayed_deletionHint: {appName} itself does not delete or overwrite backup files before the period has passed.

dialog.title: Immutability of {name}
dialog.introObjectLock: Locks every backup object written to this repository from now on with S3 Object Lock. Data already stored keeps its lock, or stays unlocked; the daily renewal also locks older data that new backups still use.
dialog.introDirectory: A directory has no Object Lock. {appName} can only delay deletion itself, and that is not immutability.
dialog.daysHintObjectLock: Restore points stay locked at least {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} after they are made. Objects are locked for {total} days (the period plus the renewal buffer) and renewed while they are in use, so their space is freed only after that.
dialog.daysHintDirectory: {appName} does not delete backup files for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} after they were written.
dialog.daysInvalid: Enter a whole number of days from {min} to {max}.
dialog.protectsObjectLock: Deleting or overwriting locked backup data before its date: by ransomware or an attacker who controls {appName}, its server or its storage access key, by a stolen administrator account, and by a retention policy that was shortened.
dialog.notProtectsObjectLock: Someone who controls {appName} can stop new backups and the renewal (what is locked stays locked until its date) and hide objects behind delete markers (the locked versions stay and can be restored). Losing the master key is not covered either, and in governance mode an account with the bypass permission.
dialog.protectsDirectory: A stolen administrator account or a shortened retention policy deleting recent backups through {appName}.
dialog.notProtectsDirectory: Anyone with access to the server, the mounter or the share can delete the files directly. For real immutability, use an S3 bucket with Object Lock, as a repository or as a copy.
dialog.governanceNote: Governance mode: give the access key of {appName} no s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission, or the lock does not hold against that key.
dialog.loweringOwnerOnly: Only the provider owner can lower or switch off immutability.
dialog.loweringNotRetroactive: It applies only to backups written from now on: everything already locked keeps its date. You will be asked to confirm that it is you.

badge.immutableHint: The storage itself confirms a compliance lock on this restore point until {date}: nobody can delete it before then.
badge.governanceHint: The storage confirms a governance lock until {date}. An account with the bypass permission could lift it.
badge.delayedHint: {appName} will not delete this restore point before {date}. This is not immutability: someone with access to the server can.
badge.noneHint: The storage reports no lock for this restore point: it was made before immutability was turned on, or its lock has run out.

destination.installationDefaultLocal: Installation default (local disk of the server)
destination.misconfigured: The installation default repository is misconfigured: backups cannot be written until the provider fixes it or a primary repository is added.

serverDisk.title: Backups land on the server's own disk
serverDisk.descriptionDefault: This tenant's backups are written to the installation default, a directory on a disk of the {appName} server itself. If the server or its disk fails, the backups are lost with it. Choose a repository elsewhere: a network share or S3-compatible object storage.
serverDisk.description: The primary repository {name} is a directory on a disk of the {appName} server itself. If the server or its disk fails, the backups are lost with it. Choose a repository elsewhere: a network share or S3-compatible object storage.

systemDisk.title: Backups land on the server's system disk
systemDisk.description: This directory is on the same disk as the operating system, Docker and the database of {appName}. When backups fill it, the database and {appName} itself stop, not only the backups. Put the repository on a second disk, a network share or object storage.
